justifications.reason: These oversized architecture-bearing files are existing legacy implementation, generated reference, or integration surfaces kept stable while the v1.8 platform/runtime boundaries are split incrementally. inc/eshkol/backend/llvm_codegen.h is the class-contract header for the already-partly-split LLVM codegen (ROADMAP.md's Codegen modularisation entry: the module-init, builtin-factory and REPL-resolution implementations already live in their own module_init_codegen.cpp / builtin_factory_codegen.cpp / repl_resolution_codegen.cpp files behind this one declaration surface). tensor_extras_codegen.cpp, tensor_codegen.cpp and tensor_shape_codegen.cpp are siblings of the already-justified tensor_{transformer,conv,reduce,activation}_codegen.cpp split files from that same v1.2 tensor_codegen.cpp decomposition (ROADMAP.md: 19,940 -> 13 focused per-domain files); they crossed the 2000-line threshold the same way their justified siblings did, through ordinary feature growth in an already-split family, not through being left unsplit. lib/core/unicode.cpp and lib/core/bignum.cpp are cohesive single-domain facades (Unicode text processing; arbitrary-precision numeric tower) in the same lib/core/ boundary as the already-justified lib/core/arena_memory.cpp and lib/core/system_builtins.c, with no ADR or roadmap item proposing a split of either.
justifications.mitigation: Keep new behavior in focused modules when practical, document exceptions during platform work, and split these files behind existing public interfaces over tracked v1.8 follow-up tasks. For the tensor_*_codegen.cpp siblings specifically, any further split follows the same per-domain-file convention the v1.2 tensor_codegen.cpp decomposition already established.

justifications.reason: complete_language_specification.html is a pandoc-generated site artifact (built from docs/COMPLETE_LANGUAGE_SPECIFICATION.md by scripts/build-site-content.sh); it is a cohesive registry of the whole language spec kept as one page for reader compatibility. inc/eshkol/eshkol.h is the single umbrella public-API facade header by design; it crossed the size threshold only because the v1.3.1 pass added Doxygen doc-comments to every public symbol (comment-only growth, code unchanged).
justifications.mitigation: The HTML is regenerated from its markdown source module on every site build, so any future split happens at the docs/ source boundary, not the generated artifact. For eshkol.h, real code growth (not comments) would be addressed by extracting subsystem headers behind the existing facade (module boundaries already exist under inc/eshkol/{core,backend,types}/); tracked with the v1.8 modular-boundaries plan.

justifications.reason: system_codegen.cpp is the cohesive registry of system/OS/FFI builtin codegen (file/process/terminal/HTTP/websocket/tree-sitter/etc.), kept as one facade so the builtin-dispatch table stays co-located. It crossed the 2000-line threshold by 6 lines solely due to the v1.3.1 Doxygen documentation pass (comment-only growth), not new logic.
justifications.mitigation: Any real code growth would be split by extracting per-domain builtin groups (fs/process/net/terminal) behind the existing dispatch facade into focused modules; tracked with the v1.8 modular-boundaries plan. Comment-driven growth needs no split.

justifications.reason: agent_subprocess.c owns one cohesive cross-platform subprocess lifecycle state machine: argument validation and quoting, spawn, pipe I/O, timeout-aware wait, termination, and destruction. Keeping that state and its Windows/POSIX parity logic together makes ownership and cleanup invariants auditable; splitting solely at the line threshold would scatter the lifecycle across translation units without creating a stable public boundary.
justifications.mitigation: Keep the lifecycle behind the existing qllm_process_* API, require the sanitizer/build-directory and hosted Windows/POSIX lanes for changes, and extract a platform backend only when it can share a typed internal process-state contract rather than duplicate cleanup logic.

justifications.reason: agent_platform.c is the existing portability facade for filesystem, time, path, text-width, encoding, hashing, and security helpers. Its public surface is stable and fully cross-platform tested, but its domains are broader than one ideal module; a release-time textual split would add linkage and platform risk without changing behavior.
justifications.mitigation: Do not add new domains to this file. During the v1.4 agent-platform boundary pass, extract filesystem/path, time/identity, terminal-text, and encoding/crypto helpers behind focused internal headers while preserving the current exported ABI and validating every extraction on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

justifications.reason: Both files are a temporary boundary held stable for the staged-dense-kernels AD architecture tracked in docs/design/adr/0002-ad-staged-dense-kernels.md: runtime_taylor.c implements the Taylor tower and reverse-over-Taylor hooks the ADR scopes directly (eshkol_taylor_lift_ad_node, eshkol_taylor_extract_tangent), and tensor_backward.cpp holds the 13 dense backward kernels and eshkol_tensor_backward_dispatch the ADR's blocker/decision tables cite by exact line (e.g. the attention-backward Q/K adjoint gap at tensor_backward.cpp:646, the silent-drop default case at 1362-1365). The ADR's own scope list names both files as in-flight; splitting them ahead of that staged plan would fork kernel groupings the ADR has not yet decided.
justifications.mitigation: No split ahead of ADR-0002's staged kernel decisions. When the ADR's blockers close (strict-mode error conversion for skipped backward kernels, attention Q/K adjoint completion, the dense-kernel staging itself), extract kernel groups along the boundaries that work settles on rather than by line count.

justifications.reason: runtime_regions.cpp is a temporary boundary held stable while docs/design/adr/0011-guest-collector-adapter.md decides the guest-collector adapter split: eshkol_current_arena() (the one allocation seam every guest collector must route through) and eshkol_region_unwind_to() (the one teardown path shared by lexical exit, explicit close, raise, and call/cc escape) are both cited from this file by exact line. The ADR is still deciding the guest-collector adapter boundary that would determine where a split, if any, belongs.
justifications.mitigation: No split ahead of ADR-0011's adapter-boundary decision. Once the guest-collector adapter contract is fixed, extract the adapter-facing seam (arena accessor, unwind path, handle protocol) behind that contract rather than splitting by line count first.

justifications.reason: riemannian_core.h is a temporary boundary, named directly in docs/design/adr/0012-signed-curvature-stereographic-geometry.md's decision-owner list ("geometry core (riemannian_core.h)"), which is actively adding the shared rho/lambda/generalized-ratio helpers and the signed stereographic forward/domain checks to this header. Splitting it before that ADR's migration lands would fork a header mid-change across the VM geometry, qLLM bridge, AD, and Moonlab integration consumers it lists as decision owners.
justifications.mitigation: No split ahead of ADR-0012 landing. Once the signed-curvature migration and its documented consumer updates (docs/reference/stdlib/geometry.md, docs/api/backend/riemannian_core.md) are complete, split the header along the chart/metric boundary that migration establishes.

justifications.reason: vm_prelude_cache.h is machine-generated bytecode data, not authored source: it opens with "Auto-generated by vm_prelude_cache.c -- DO NOT EDIT" and its entire body is a cohesive registry of three static data tables (prelude_ops, plus the matching constant/local tables) produced by eshkol-vm-prelude-cache-gen from the compiled stdlib prelude. It has 1 symbol and 1 function by construction. CMakeLists.txt wires a staleness gate (the vm_prelude_cache generator + gate, SW-49) that fails the build if this file drifts from what the generator would produce now, so its content is already mechanically verified on every build -- a line-count threshold measuring hand-authored complexity does not apply to a generated data blob.
justifications.mitigation: None needed: this file must stay whatever size the generator emits. If it should ever be edited by hand, that already violates the DO NOT EDIT contract and the CI staleness gate; the modularity threshold is not the relevant control here.

justifications.reason: pjrt_c_api.h is an unmodified, vendored third-party header ("Copyright 2022 The OpenXLA Authors", Apache License 2.0) defining the PJRT plugin C ABI this repo's XLA/TPU backend links against for compatibility with upstream's own versioning. It is not Eshkol source code and this repo does not own its structure: PJRT_STRUCT_SIZE-style ABI definitions, struct layouts and the full C API surface are upstream's design, kept as one file to match how OpenXLA ships and versions it.
justifications.mitigation: Do not hand-edit; refresh by re-vendoring the upstream file on a version bump (see deps/pjrt/) rather than splitting it, so future re-vendoring stays a clean file replacement instead of a merge across split fragments.
